s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of loss of consciousness with neck and back pain, associated with abnormal cardiac rhythms and family history of sudden cardiac death
salient_findings: Abnormal cardiac rhythms, including complete atrioventricular block and junctional escape rhythm
Family history of sudden cardiac death
key_facts: Patient is a 47-year-old woman with controllable hypertension
Presented with neck and back pain and loss of consciousness
Had a similar episode one year prior
Family history of sudden cardiac death in uncle and two sisters
Took calcium channel blocker for one month after first episode
Body temperature was 37.5°C on admission
Heart rate was 68 bpm on admission
Blood pressure was 145/50 mmHg on admission
Pupils were equal at 3.5 mm with sluggish light reflex
Absent corneal reflex
Normal lung auscultation
Mild hyperglycemia (11.92 mmol/L) on laboratory tests
Elevated transaminases (ALT 146 U/L, AST 89 U/L) on laboratory tests
Arterial blood gas showed pH 7.213, PCO2 35.8 mmHg, PO2 396.1 mmHg, HCO3− 14.1 mmol/L, O2 saturation 99.7%, lactate 11.53 mmol/L
Initial troponin I, D-dimer, and BNP levels were normal
Head and chest CT scans were unremarkable
Coronary angiography revealed normal left and right coronary arteries
Left ventricular ejection fraction was 59%
ECG showed complete atrioventricular block with inferior ST-segment elevation (heart rate 45 bpm) during first episode
ECG showed junctional escape rhythm (heart rate 32 bpm) during second episode
Whole exome sequencing performed on patient and family members showed no abnormalities

shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal cardiac rhythms and family history of sudden cardiac death

shortlist.why_kept: Complete atrioventricular block and junctional escape rhythm on ECG

shortlist.why_kept: Family history of sudden cardiac death and abnormal cardiac rhythms

raw.rationale: The patient's family history of sudden cardiac death, episodes of loss of consciousness, and ECG findings of complete atrioventricular block with inferior ST-segment elevation and junctional escape rhythm are consistent with Long QT syndrome, which can cause life-threatening arrhythmias and is often associated with a family history of sudden cardiac death.

rejected.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: While this condition can cause arrhythmias, the patient's ECG findings and family history are more suggestive of Long QT syndrome.

rejected.label: Brugada syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's ECG findings do not show the characteristic ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3 that is typical of Brugada syndrome.

rejected.label: Progressive cardiac conduction defect
rejected.why: The patient's ECG findings are more suggestive of an arrhythmia disorder such as Long QT syndrome rather than a progressive conduction defect.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's imaging studies, including coronary angiography and left ventricular ejection fraction, do not show evidence of right ventricular dysfunction or fibrofatty replacement that is characteristic of this condition.
